chunks: Look! They have chosen for themselves one who is nearest of all of them to what they desire,
while you have chosen one who is nearest to what you dislike.
You may certainly recall that the other day ‘Abdullāh ibn Qays (Abū Mūsā) was saying: “It is a mischief, therefore, cut away your bow-string and sheathe your swords.”
If he was right (in what he said) then he was wrong in marching (with us) without being forced,
but if he was lying then he should be viewed with suspicion.
Therefore, send ‘Abdullāh ibn al-‘Abbās to face ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ.
Make use of these days and
Do you not see that your cities are being attacked and your prowess is being aimed at?
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the arbitration reference in Imam Ali's sermon after Siffin?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) critiques the political maneuvering of the opposing party, highlighting the irony that they selected arbitrators based on personal preference rather than merit, leading to the stalemate of the Siffin arbitration. He invokes the warning of Abd Allah ibn Qays regarding the 'fitnah' of arbitration and strategically proposes sending the learned Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas to negotiate with Amr ibn al-As, aiming to preserve the core tenets of Islam while addressing the urgent threat of external invasion. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly view of the arbitration as a political compromise that delayed but did not prevent the eventual shift in authority.
